model_scope: A finite, mass-bearing continuum framework in which matter/Sintot, HDF, LDF propagation, gravitational attraction, redshift, lensing, compact-object saturation, and gravitational-wave energy release are different regimes of one medium/state system.
git_status: No Git repository existed while Domains M, N, R, S, T-IVP, U, U2, and V were run. This commit is the first reproducible archive point after the fact, NOT the commit that generated the earlier results.

substrate.statement: Space is not treated as physical nothing. The baseline is a finite, mass-bearing HDF/LDF medium with state-dependent density, stress, propagation geometry, and compressibility.

sintot.statement: Sintot is organized/condensed medium inventory. Matter is a stable organized state of the same underlying medium, not an unrelated ontological substance.

conservation.statement: Matter-energy is not created from nothing, destroyed at a singularity, or sent through a required separate universe. It reorganizes among condensed Sintot, bound/compressed HDF, baseline HDF, propagating LDF, and outward HDF/gravity-wave modes.

gravity.statement: More locally concentrated HDF medium corresponds to greater pull.
gravity.status: PWC premise / required exterior constraint, not yet independently derived from a medium functional

lensing.statement: LDF/light follows locally straight available paths through curved or inhomogeneous HDF geometry. Bending is path guidance, not necessarily ordinary refractive drag or sub-local-limit photon slowing.
lensing.status: PWC premise, no ray-equation derivation performed in this session

redshift.statement: HDF density state determines local process constraint. Emission from denser HDF observed in lower-density HDF/LDF is redshifted relative to the receiver's local process standard.
redshift.status: PWC premise, no explicit state-to-process mapping derived or tested in this session

compact_objects.statement: A compact object is a finite high-density HDF/Sintot core plus a continuously descending compressed-HDF envelope.

hdf_max_density.provenance: PWC compact-object constraint, distinct from neutron/nuclear matter density -- this distinction was itself the subject of a real correction earlier in this session

mergers.statement: In a merger, compact-core inventory remains accounted for; the outgoing gravity-wave mass equivalent is released excess compressed/bound HDF field inventory.
mergers.required_refinement: The emitted fraction depends on the full radial density-envelope structure, relative sizes, overlap geometry, and spin/flow state -- NOT a universal one-constant mass-only fraction. A frozen one-constant version was tested (k~0.8525, and separately f~0.04594) and did not transfer to held-out events (GW190412) -- see excluded_substitutions.
mergers.status: PWC premise for the identity; the specific frozen-fraction proxy is REJECTED, not the premise itself

mass_baseline.statement: Establishes that the baseline HDF medium has inertial mass because it contains light energy.
mass_baseline.honest_note: Algebraically identical to E=mc^2 rearranged (m=E/c^2) -- not a new equation. The PWC-specific content is the interpretation: L is specifically identified as light/HDF energy (not energy in the abstract), and c0^2 is read as the medium's own conversion threshold. Consistent with how this project has flagged other cases tonight where a relation matches known physics exactly (e.g. the D=4GM/c^2 compact-object diameter, identical to the Schwarzschild diameter) -- the number/equation is not new, the ontological reading of it is.

bookkeeping_constraint.statement: All subsequent HDF/LDF/Sintot mechanics must preserve this bookkeeping baseline. Any energy released or absorbed as light corresponds to a mass change.
bookkeeping_constraint.sign_convention: Delta_M > 0 for the system when it absorbs light energy (Delta_L > 0 absorbed); Delta_M < 0 for the system when it emits light energy (Delta_L > 0 emitted). Sign is set by whether the defined system is emitting or absorbing, not by an independent convention.

excluded_substitutions.status: Rejected: the true rule requires profile and overlap geometry; the frozen-fraction proxy failed a held-out test (GW190412) earlier this session.

excluded_substitutions.statement: PWC requires an empty exterior, singularity, dark-halo particle, or another universe.
excluded_substitutions.status: Rejected: contradicts the stated finite-medium ledger.

diffuse_isothermal_HDF_branch.verification: Derived analytically (this session) and independently confirmed numerically via Domain V's baryon-free control run (see surrogate_and_numerical_audits.domains.V), which reproduced the predicted asymptotic slope (-2.02 to -2.51 near the outer boundary, target -2) via an actual solve_bvp integration, not by assumption.
assumptions: low-density EOS becomes isothermal: P_excess ~ c_s^2*rho_excess
diffuse_isothermal_HDF_branch.important_scope: Analytic existence/asymptotic derivation, numerically confirmed ONLY in the baryon-free control case. Whether the full baryon-coupled, finite-disk boundary problem selects this branch for real galaxies is UNRESOLVED -- Domain V's real-galaxy convergence test found multiple competing solution branches, not a clean selection of this one.

The SPECIFIC numbers claimed (36.2+29.1->62.3 Msun, ~5.4e47 J) do not appear in PWC.md or pwc_gw150914_pipeline.py, and no results file with these exact figures was located.

compact_K_scan_parameter_reconciliation.status: RESOLVED -- different physical variable, different model era
compact_K_scan_parameter_reconciliation.method: Full read of both scripts + grep for hdf/sintot/neutron/core (zero occurrences in either) + file date comparison
compact_K_scan_parameter_reconciliation.reference_point: PWC/dynamic_knot_solver.py (2026-09-13) -- where the HDF/LDF/Sintot vocabulary and rho_HDF_max=4.6e10 parameter actually originate, 3 days AFTER the compact scripts
compact_K_scan_parameter_reconciliation.finding: Neither compact script contains the words hdf, sintot, neutron, or core anywhere -- they predate that vocabulary entirely. Their own comments and physical setup (real degenerate/incompressible matter, GW150914-relevant total mass ~28-36 Msun, radii checked in the tens-of-km range) unambiguously describe compact-object/nuclear-density-scale core material -- 4.6e17 kg/m^3 sits at the nuclear saturation density scale. This is a categorically different physical regime from the diffuse, kpc-scale galactic medium parameter (rho_HDF_max=4.6e10) used in tonight galaxy-scale work.
compact_K_scan_parameter_reconciliation.conclusion: Combination of reconciliation explanations 1 and 3: a genuinely different density variable (compact/degenerate core density vs diffuse HDF medium density) from an earlier model version/vocabulary, not a transcription error and not a genuine parameter conflict -- neither script asserts these are the same quantity.
compact_K_scan_parameter_reconciliation.remaining_action: Neither script gives its rho_max an explicit, disambiguated name (e.g. rho_Sintot_max or rho_core_max) -- recommended naming fix for future work, not a retroactive claim about what these scripts already say.
compact_K_scan_parameter_reconciliation.additional_finding_retained: Independent of the naming question, running both scripts directly still does not reproduce the specific claimed "~1.5% stable across an eightfold K scan": stiffening_K_scan.py shows R_envelope varying from 0.006 km to 19053.7 km (6+ orders of magnitude) across K=1e7 to 1e20.
